title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.32888v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. translated_title: 当人类纠偏数据迁移时：联邦VLA适配中的安全性
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略能够适应本地的人类干预，而联邦学习可以在不汇集原始记录的情况下整合分布式机器人经验。我们考察了两者未来的交叉点：共享由多样化的人类纠偏所衍生、跨任务、环境、人员和机器人本体的适配更新。纠偏在模态、安全语义（紧迫性、行为范围等）和隐私敏感性方面各不相同。一个提升平均任务成功率的共享更新，可能抑制罕见的安全干预，或在另一台机器人上产生不安全的响应。我们提出三项要求：在决定共享内容时保留多模态纠偏的上下文与不确定性；在部署前于每台接收机器人的闭环中评估候选更新；以及在评估信息泄露的同时评估安全关键证据的保留。在人类交互期间，即时、清晰可读的防御行为仍然是必要的。我们提供了对……
tldr: 论文提出在联邦学习框架下共享人类纠偏衍生的VLA适配更新时，必须保留多模态纠偏的上下文与不确定性、在接收机器人闭环中预先评估更新、并兼顾隐私泄露与安全关键证据的保留，从而确保跨任务、环境与机器人本体的安全适配。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes three requirements—preserving the context and uncertainty of multimodal human corrections, validating candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop, and jointly evaluating privacy leakage and retention of safety-critical evidence—to ensure safe federated sharing of VLA adaptations across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments.
